axes.model_access:
**Uses Google's own Gemini family**; models can be switched.
The context ceiling is explicitly stated as 1M tokens.

**README first-screen wording**: "Powerful Gemini 3 models: Access to improved reasoning
and 1M token context window"

**Switching models**: specify via `gemini -m gemini-2.5-flash` on the command line.
When signing in with a Gemini API Key, the official description is:

**"Model selection**: Choose specific Gemini models"

**Three access modes** (README "Authentication Options"):

- **Google account OAuth login** — the free tier uses this: 60 requests/min, 1,000 requests/day, no key to manage
- **Gemini API Key** — get a key in AI Studio, pay per usage
- **Vertex AI** — for enterprises, requires a project and region

**Model routing**: Plan Mode can use `general.plan.modelRouting`.
It switches automatically between Pro (planning) and Flash (implementation).
There is also experimental Local Model Routing (Gemma).

**The exact list of switchable models on the CLI side and their version mapping: the official docs do not give a complete list.**
(Repository docs and the reference/configuration page both checked.)
axes.runtime:
**A local process, running in the terminal, launchable without installation via npx.**

The official docs make "no installation" a first-screen selling point of the repository — this is how it lowers the entry barrier.

**README wording**: "Using npx (no installation required)"
axes.local_files:
**Built-in file tools default to the workspace as root, with a clear boundary.**

**Official "File system tools" page wording**: All file system tools operate within a
`rootDirectory` (the current working directory or workspace root) for security

Tool set:

- `list_directory`
- `read_file` — supports text / images / audio / PDF
- `write_file`
- `replace`
- `glob`
- `grep_search`

Which ones need your nod to act:

- `write_file` and `replace` — officially marked "Requires manual user approval"

**Extending directories**: launch with
`gemini --include-directories ../lib,../docs`.
Within a session use `/directory add <path>` (disabled under restricted sandbox configs).

**Ignore boundary**: respects `.gitignore`, and supports `.geminiignore` with the same syntax.

**Changes are revertible**: when you approve a file-changing tool, the CLI commits a snapshot.
It lands in a shadow Git repository, not interfering with your own project repo.
`/restore` reverts.

**The repo location recorded on the checkpointing page**: `~/.gemini/history/<project_hash>`

**Original wording**: "It does **not** interfere with your own project's Git repository"

**The semantic-indexing (Code Customization / RAG) algorithm and large-repo time cost are not stated officially.**
(file-system and configuration pages checked; only debug switches like `general.logRagSnippets` exist.)
axes.background:
**A local CLI; it cannot keep running after shutdown.**

**Non-interactive / headless is scripting, not background.** It still runs on your own machine.

**Official "Headless mode" page wording**: "Headless mode provides a programmatic
interface to Gemini CLI... without an interactive terminal UI"

Triggers:

- non-TTY environments
- `-p/--prompt`

Output can be JSON or stream-json for CI and automation to consume.

**The execution environment is yours**: the official docs provide no vendor-hosted resident execution environment.
The GitHub Action in the repository also runs on your repo's CI runners.

**Interruption is recoverable**: checkpointing and `/chat save` / `/resume`
can save and restore sessions.
The switch is `general.checkpointing.enabled`.
`general.sessionRetention` defaults to 30 days.
Expired sessions are cleaned up automatically.

**Quota** is exactly the daily request ceilings in the official usage policy.
The official docs set no separate cloud quota.
axes.tools:
**MCP is explicitly supported and is one of its headline features.**

**README wording**: "🔌 Extensible: MCP (Model Context Protocol) support for
custom capabilities"

MCP has its own docs page: `/docs/tools/mcp-server`.
The example it gives is using MCP to connect multimodal generation:

"Use MCP servers to connect new capabilities, including media generation
with Imagen, Veo or Lyria"

This example deserves its own note: here MCP is not just connecting tools,
it can also connect Google's multimodal generation capabilities (image / video / audio).
This usage is not emphasized on the first screen of other CLI tools' repositories.

Built-in tool list:

- **Google Search grounding**
- **shell**

There is also **non-interactive mode for script automation**. The official docs have a dedicated section
**"Non-interactive mode for scripts"**.
axes.context:
**1M-token context + layered GEMINI.md context + automatic history compression — all three have dedicated official pages.**

**Context window**: the README first screen says Gemini 3 models with 1M token context window.

**Context layers** (official "GEMINI.md" page):

- ① global `~/.gemini/GEMINI.md`
- ② `GEMINI.md` in workspace directories and their parents
- ③ JIT — when a tool accesses a directory, it scans that directory's and its ancestors' `GEMINI.md` (up to the trusted root)

The file name can be changed via `context.fileName` (e.g. AGENTS.md / CONTEXT.md).

**GEMINI.md page**: supports imports via `@file.md` syntax.
`/memory show` and `/memory reload` inspect and reload.

**Compaction strategy verified** (official core page):

"When a conversation approaches the token limit... the core automatically
compresses the conversation history"

The threshold is controlled by `model.compressionThreshold`.
The default is 0.5.
You can also `/compress` to manually replace the whole context with a summary.

**Cross-session memory**: the official Memory tool writes durable facts into `GEMINI.md` (project / global two levels),
injected into later sessions via the layered context. Token caching is only available to API key / Vertex users.
axes.permissions:
**Sandbox, approvals and trusted folders each have dedicated official pages — the most finely documented permission surface in this section.**

**Sandbox**: the official "Sandboxing" page gives these mechanisms.

- macOS Seatbelt — default profile `permissive-open`: deny by default, writes limited to the project directory, but reads and network allowed
- Docker / Podman
- native Windows
- gVisor / runsc
- LXC / LXD (experimental)

Enabling:

- `-s/--sandbox`
- `GEMINI_SANDBOX`
- `tools.sandbox`

Tool-level additionally has `security.toolSandboxing`.

**Sandbox expansion**: when a command fails due to permission limits, a
**"Sandbox Expansion Request"** pops up. Approving case by case relaxes it temporarily.
Out-of-bounds directories can be mounted via `SANDBOX_MOUNTS`.

**Approval modes** (configuration page): `general.defaultApprovalMode`
has three values:

- `default` — ask each time
- `auto_edit`
- `plan` — read-only

`--yolo` (auto-approve everything) can only be enabled on the command line.

**Policy engine** ("Policy engine" page): `~/.gemini/policies/*.toml`
defines `allow` / `deny` / `ask_user` via rules.
Match conditions can key on tool name, arguments, approval mode, and interactive / non-interactive environment.
Rules have four tiers: Default / Extension / User / Admin.
Admin can force-override.

**Trusted Folders**: **off by default**.
The switch is `security.folderTrust.enabled`.
When untrusted it enters safe mode — ignoring workspace `.gemini/settings.json` and `.env`,
disabling tool auto-accept, not connecting MCP, not loading custom commands.
To bypass in CI there are two routes:

- `--skip-trust`
- `GEMINI_CLI_TRUST_WORKSPACE=true`

The configuration page also has an environment-variable redaction section.
axes.fit:
Fits three scenarios:

- wanting an install-free quick trial (npx, leaving no installation trace)
- needing MCP extensions, especially wiring Gemini's multimodal generation (Imagen / Veo / Lyria) into an agent workflow
- needing scripted non-interactive runs, e.g. wiring into CI

Three more kinds of people also fit:

- those needing a large context window — 1M tokens, one of the few in this section with an explicit ceiling stated
- those needing a "changes are revertible" guarantee — shadow-Git checkpoints plus `/restore`
- those needing a project-level standing instruction file — GEMINI.md

**Not a fit** for treating the quota as unlimited.
The free tier has explicit daily ceilings: 6,000 code requests + 240 chats/day.
And CLI and proxy-mode quotas are counted together.

sections.三个明确的工程化能力:
### ① npx, no installation

> README wording: "Using npx (no installation required)"

This is a design that lowers the usage barrier — good for quick trials or temporary use, leaving no installation trace locally.

### ② MCP support is an officially labeled core feature

**MCP is marked as a core feature**, symbolized by that plug icon:

> "🔌 Extensible: MCP (Model Context Protocol) support for custom capabilities"

**It also uses MCP to connect multimodal generation**:

> "Use MCP servers to connect new capabilities, including media generation with Imagen, Veo or Lyria"

**This example deserves its own note**: MCP here is not just connecting tools;
it can also connect Google's multimodal generation capabilities (image / video / audio).
This is a usage other CLI tools do not emphasize on their repository first screens.

The official docs have a dedicated page: `/docs/tools/mcp-server`

### ③ Non-interactive mode

The README has a dedicated section **"Non-interactive mode for scripts"**, positioned as workflow automation.

**This is the only one of the three CLI tools that spells out non-interactive capability on the repository first screen** — a signal of CI-integration friendliness.

sections.值得单独记的两处:
### ① Checkpoints use shadow Git, not polluting your repo

When you approve a file-changing tool (`write_file` / `replace`), the CLI commits a snapshot.

- the snapshot repo lives at `~/.gemini/history/<project_hash>`
- it is a **separate Git repository**; it will not touch your project repo
- to revert, use `/restore`

The source is the checkpointing doc:

> original wording: "It does **not** interfere with your own project's Git repository"

This is one of the few in this section that builds the "safety net" into the mechanism —
most tools rely on "auto-committing into your repo" or "letting you undo yourself".

### ② GEMINI.md is the project-level standing instruction

It is like writing "how this project does things" into a file;
multiple forms (CLI / VS Code / JetBrains) all read it.
This is the same class of mechanism as Cline's `.clinerules` and Claude Code's CLAUDE.md — **worth a cross-tool comparison**.
